To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the integral method with an automatic ROI is a more accurate and more stable method than the slope method for measuring the glomerular filtration rates (GFRs) using 99mTctc-diethylenetriamine pentaacetic acid (DTPA) renography; (ii) the GFR measured by 99mtc-DTPA renography is comparable to that measured by plasma clearance of 99mtcDTPA;

the best correlation between GFR by 99m Tc-DTPA clearance and GFR by 2 methods of uptake of 9mTc-DPTA scintigraphy was derived from time interval between 30s to 120s with a background ROI at 3 pixels out from the automatic kidney ROI using automatic ROIs at a 20% threshold for integral method and 35% threshold for slope method.

The percentage dose uptake method is a more accurate and stable method to estimate GFR than the slope method, and that both methods are more accurate and stable when the background ROI is at 2 pixels outside the kidney ROI and the kidney ROI is automatically drawn using a 35% threshold.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of region of interest (ROI), uptake measurement and uptake phase of the 99mTcu DTPA scintiscan on glomerular function rate (GFR).
the effect of region of interest (ROI), the method of uptake measurement and the duration of uptake phase on the glomerular filtration rates (GFR) measured by 99 mTc-DTPAscintigraphy in dogs.
the effect of region of interest (ROI), and uptake measurement of glomerular function measured by 99Tc-DTPa scintigraphy in healthy dogs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DTPA renograms are accurate and reliable for the measurement of GFR, but the integral method is more accurate and stable than the slope method.
the percentage DTPA renal uptake method with automatic ROIs is the preferred method of GFR estimation by 99m Tc-DTPA renography.
the percentage uptake method is more accurate and reliable than the slope uptake method for measuring the GFR in dogs using 99mTcd-DTPA renography.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a single 99mTcdTPA renogram with a 2 minute uptake period, followed by an excretion phase, is a reliable, rapid, non-invasive method to measure GFR.

for the integral method the optimal time period of 30s-60s and for the slope method 30s-45s are sufficient to estimate the GSR with a high accuracy and that the background ROI should be placed at 1 pixel out from the kidney.
the integral method using the percentage dose uptake is the preferred method of GFR estimation with 99mT Tc-DTPA renography.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the slope method is not recommended for GFR measurement using DTPA renograms.
the integral method using a background correction is more accurate and reliable than the slope method in estimating GFR.
the integral method of GFR estimation is more reliable than the slope method and that the use of automatic background and kidney ROIs is superior to manual background and kidney ROI.
